sections.title: Growth & Statutory Earnings
sections.subtitle: Revenue is the clean compounding series; statutory net income below is dominated by IAS-40 fair-value movements and impairments, not operating performance

charts.title: Statutory Net Income (incl. fair-value movements)
charts.annotation: Includes IAS-40 fair-value gains/losses on the $10.9bn investment-property portfolio plus impairments ($243.6m FY2024, $172.9m FY2025). FY2025's -$513.7m and FY2026's -$171.3m are NOT operating losses of that scale -- they reflect muted/negative fair-value movements on a book that is still growing in cash terms. Never used as a P/E input here.

charts.title: Statutory EPS (cents)
charts.annotation: EPS is reported in CENTS, not dollars. Two dilutive raises changed the share base (500m to FY2022, 688m FY2023-24, 1,015.7m FY2025+) -- do not compare FY2021 EPS of 84.6c against FY2026's -16.9c as like-for-like; the denominator more than doubled.

sections.title: Cash Flow & Deleveraging
sections.subtitle: The live thesis: falling development CapEx and debt paydown produced the first genuinely positive free cash flow in a decade

charts.title: Operating Cash Flow, CapEx & Free Cash Flow
charts.annotation: Operating Cash Flow is NOT free cash flow for an ORA operator: it is inflated by resident occupation-advance receipts (a financing-like inflow) that must be continuously redeployed into new-unit construction. CapEx collapsed from $535.9m (FY2025) to $221.8m (FY2026) as management paused development -- this, not an operating improvement alone, is what pushed Free Cash Flow to +$112.2m in FY2026.

charts.title: Total Debt vs Shareholders' Equity
charts.annotation: Reported TotalDebt (FY2026 $1,581.0m) differs slightly from management's own 'net interest-bearing debt' KPI ($1,650.8m at H1 FY2026, down from a $2,548m FY2022 peak) due to netting conventions; both tell the same deleveraging story. A new 1.50x Interest Cover Ratio covenant starts Sept-2026.

charts.title: Dividend per Share
charts.annotation: Dividend suspended from FY2023 onward (zero shown/blank thereafter). Management targets a return to sustainable dividends in FY2028 at 20-50% of cash flow from existing operations, conditional on continued execution.

sections.title: Balance Sheet & Margins
sections.subtitle: Book value per share (NTA) is the central valuation anchor for this ORA/DMF operator -- see the DCF section below for how it drives the intrinsic value

charts.title: Shareholders' Equity & Total Assets
charts.annotation: Total Assets keep growing (the $10.9bn investment-property portfolio) while Shareholders' Equity has fallen since FY2023 despite two large capital raises, because fair-value losses and impairments have outpaced new capital and retained earnings.

charts.title: Net Margin (Statutory)
charts.annotation: Swings entirely with IAS-40 fair-value movements, not the underlying cost base -- read alongside the Statutory Net Income chart, not as an operating efficiency signal.

charts.title: Cash & Equivalents
charts.annotation: Ryman runs a lean cash balance and manages liquidity through committed bank facilities (refinanced to ~$2bn in Nov-2025, no bank maturities until FY31) rather than holding cash reserves.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Total operating revenue: care and village weekly fees (63%), deferred management fees (DMF, 19%), imputed interest income on resident loans/RADs (6%) and other income (2%). This is NOT the value of Occupation Right Agreements (ORAs) sold -- ORA capital is a refundable resident-loan liability on the balance sheet, not revenue.

For Ryman: revenue has compounded from $342.5m (FY2018) to $855.6m (FY2026), up 13% in FY2026 alone, and is the cleanest growth series in the business -- unlike net income, it is not distorted by IAS-40 fair-value swings. Repricing of the resident book (standard DMF lifted to 30%, weekly-fee uplifts of ~60% on rollovers) is mechanically lifting the yield on this line even before any volume growth, as the ~12%/year portfolio turnover works through.

What to watch:

  • Whether the DMF repricing (20.7% to 30% in one year) continues to flow through as older contracts turn over
  • ORA sales volumes (1,410 in FY2026, guided 1,300-1,400) as a leading indicator of future fee income, even though sales proceeds themselves don't appear here

netIncome.title: Statutory Net Income (incl. fair-value movements)
netIncome.content:
What is an ORA? Ryman sells Occupation Right Agreements: residents pay an upfront occupation advance for the right to occupy a unit. That advance is booked as a refundable resident-loan liability, not revenue. Ryman instead earns a Deferred Management Fee (DMF) accrued over the resident's tenure, plus any capital gain on resale. Statutory net profit also includes IAS-40 fair-value (revaluation) movements on the ~$10.9bn investment-property portfolio and any impairments.

For Ryman: this is why statutory NPAT swung from +$4.8m (FY2024) to -$513.7m (FY2025) to -$171.3m (FY2026) -- fair-value gains that used to flatter reported profit collapsed as the NZ/Victoria housing market flattened, and large impairments ($243.6m FY2024, $172.9m FY2025) were booked on top. None of this is a cash operating loss of that magnitude. Do NOT price this stock on a P/E multiple or read this line as a trading-performance trend -- management itself abandoned 'Underlying Profit' in FY2024 for the same reason and now reports Operating EBITDAF and Free Cash Flow instead.

What to watch:

  • Whether fair-value movements turn positive again as the housing market stabilises (the base-case DCF assumes only a partial recovery)
  • Operating EBITDAF and Free Cash Flow (charted elsewhere) as the cleaner operating signals

eps.title: Statutory EPS (cents)
eps.content:
Statutory earnings per share, reported in NEW ZEALAND CENTS (not dollars). Inherits all the fair-value/impairment noise described in the Net Income metric.

For Ryman: two dilutive equity raises broke the per-share history: shares outstanding were 500m through FY2022, rose to 688m after the ~$902m FY2023 raise, and jumped to 1,015.7m after the ~$970m Feb-2025 raise. A reader comparing FY2021's +84.6c against FY2026's -16.9c is not comparing like-for-like -- the share count more than doubled in between, so even an unchanged dollar profit would show roughly half the EPS.

What to watch:

  • Always read this alongside the Shares Outstanding KPI card before drawing any per-share conclusion
  • FY2026's loss per share (-16.9c) improved materially from FY2025 (-72.3c) even on a larger share count -- a genuine improvement, not a dilution artefact

cashFlow.title: Operating Cash Flow, CapEx & Free Cash Flow
cashFlow.content:
Operating Cash Flow (OCF), capital expenditure, and Free Cash Flow (OCF less CapEx) as reported.

For Ryman: OCF is NOT free cash flow available to shareholders for an ORA/DMF operator. It is substantially inflated by cash receipts from new ORA sales and resales -- capital-like inflows that must be continuously redeployed into building new units, not distributable earnings. This is exactly why the DCF for this company discounts a book-value (NTA) path rather than OCF or reported FCF. That said, the trend in reported Free Cash Flow is still informative: CapEx fell from $535.9m (FY2025) to $221.8m (FY2026) as management deliberately reduced the number of villages under construction from seven to two, and the resulting +$112.2m Free Cash Flow (company's own measure: +$188.3m) is the first full-year positive figure in over a decade.

What to watch:

  • Whether the FY2029 targets (at least $500m cumulative cash release, $150m sustainable cash-flow improvement) continue to be delivered as guided
  • Do not treat OCF alone as owner earnings -- always look at the OCF-less-CapEx or company FCF measure instead

debtEquity.title: Total Debt vs Shareholders' Equity
debtEquity.content:
Total interest-bearing debt against shareholders' equity at each period end.

For Ryman: this chart is the deleveraging thesis in one picture. Management's own 'net interest-bearing debt' KPI peaked at $2,548m (FY2022) and has fallen to $1,650.8m (H1 FY2026) as development slowed and resales/land sales generated cash. Gearing fell from ~45% (Sep-2022) to ~28% (Mar-2026). A full refinancing of ~$2bn of syndicated bank facilities (Nov-2025) extended average tenor to ~4.8-5 years with no bank maturities until FY31.

What to watch:

  • A new 1.50x Interest Cover Ratio covenant starts September 2026 -- a renewed housing downturn or cash-flow setback could pressure headroom despite the refinancing
  • Shareholders' equity has fallen even as debt has fallen, because fair-value losses have outpaced the two large capital raises -- deleveraging alone does not guarantee book-value recovery

dividend.title: Dividend per Share
dividend.content:
Total dividend declared per share for the fiscal year.

For Ryman: the dividend has been suspended since FY2023 as the balance-sheet reset took priority over distributions, meaning income-focused holders have gone roughly five years without a payout. Management has now set an explicit target to resume dividends in FY2028, at a payout ratio of 20-50% of cash flow from existing operations (CFEO) per share -- the DCF's base and bull cases model a resumption on this schedule; the bear case keeps it suspended through FY2031.

What to watch:

  • Any signal at FY2027 results on whether the FY2028 resumption timeline is holding
  • The eventual payout ratio chosen within the 20-50% CFEO range, since it directly drives the dividend component of the DCF's per-share value

equity.title: Shareholders' Equity & Total Assets
equity.content:
Total shareholders' equity (net assets) versus total assets at each period end.

For Ryman: Total Assets keep growing -- driven by the $10.9bn investment-property portfolio (up from $4.4bn in FY2018) -- while Shareholders' Equity has actually fallen from a $4,664m FY2023 peak to $4,077.7m in FY2026, despite two large capital raises injecting roughly $1.87bn combined. Fair-value losses and impairments have outpaced both organic retained earnings and the raised capital. Net Tangible Assets per share (a related, non-CSV KPI tracked by management) fell from 669.6c (FY2022) to 406c (H1 FY2026) -- more than the raw equity figure, because of dilution.

What to watch:

  • NTA per share is the central valuation anchor for this stock: at a $2.13 price against ~$4.01-4.06 of NTA, Ryman trades around 0.53x book, near the bottom of its 10-year 0.53x-2.64x range
  • Whether equity stabilises and begins compounding again as fair-value movements normalise, per the DCF's base case

netMargin.title: Net Margin (Statutory)
netMargin.content:
Statutory net income as a percentage of revenue.

For Ryman: this ratio is driven almost entirely by the same IAS-40 fair-value movements and impairments that distort the Net Income line -- it swung from +136.2% (FY2022, a year of large fair-value gains) to -67.5% (FY2025). It says essentially nothing about the underlying cost efficiency of running the villages and should not be read as an operating margin.

What to watch:

  • Operating EBITDAF margin (a management non-GAAP measure not in this CSV) is the more useful operating-efficiency gauge, and it nearly doubled in FY2026
  • Direction of travel (loss narrowing from -67.5% to -20.0%) matters more than the absolute level given the noise in this line

cash.title: Cash & Equivalents
cash.content:
Cash and cash equivalents held at each period end.

For Ryman: cash is run deliberately lean (as low as $8.9m at FY2026) because liquidity is managed through committed bank facilities rather than a cash buffer -- consistent with a capital-intensive, debt-funded development model. The November 2025 refinancing of ~$2bn of syndicated facilities (average tenor ~4.8-5 years, no bank maturities until FY31) is the more meaningful liquidity signal than the cash balance shown here.

What to watch:

  • Undrawn facility headroom (not shown in this CSV) alongside the new 1.50x Interest Cover Ratio covenant starting Sept-2026
